cognate: Arm. towr (acc. pl. towrs) = Gk δῶρον = Slav. darъ (Serb. дар) < *déh₃-ro-; Arm. tal (inf. of tam) = Gk δίδωμι = Slav. dati < *deh₃-
shared_syntax: figura etymologica: verb *deh₃- 'give' + accusative object *deh₃-ro- 'gift' (Arm. towrs tal, Gk δῶρα δίδωμι / δῶρον δοῦναι, Serb. даре дати)
context: giving gifts: Armenian = Nerses' charity (towrs tal beside ołormowtʻiwn ar̄nel); Greek = guest-gift (Od. 1.316), gifts to a ruler/bribe (Hdt.). Context only loosely congruent; the noun *déh₃ro- is confined to Greek, Armenian and Balto-Slavic and in all three is construed with its own verb
note: Defensible only as a shared figura on a lexeme restricted to Gk/Arm/BSl; a cognate accusative of this kind is easily regenerated, and the Armenian is Christian prose with biblical models (Matt 7:11 δόματα διδόναι).

near_miss.lead: bound by feet and hands: Arm. kapeal otiwkʻ ew kapeal jer̄awkʻ (*pṓds + *ǵʰésr̥) ~ Gk πόδας καὶ χεῖρε
near_miss.why_not: Od. 12.442 in the slab is not binding. A real Armenian formula (also Agathangelos, Lazar), and Homer binds 'hands and feet' (Od. 12.50, 12.178, 22.189), but the binding verbs are not cognate and the Armenian has a direct biblical model (Matt 22:13, John 11:44 δεδεμένος τοὺς πόδας καὶ τὰς χεῖρας, quoted by Mambre); merism ubiquitous.
